title_original: Willa, Women Make Movies Team to Release Shalini Kantayya’s Doc ‘Love Apptually’ Theatrically

blocks.text: Willa and Women Make Movies have teamed up to distribute documentary “ Love Apptually ,” theatrically in the U.S. Set for a February released timed to Valentine’s Day, “Love Apptually,” directed by Shalini Kantayya, follows French journalist Judith Duportail’s journey from her early fascination with Tinder to an investigation into the technologies and business incentives mediating our search for human connection. After uncovering Tinder’s hidden desirability rating system, Duportail demanded access to her personal data, ultimately receiving 800 pages of information collected by the platform. What begins as a personal curiosity evolves into a global investigation into how a multi-billion-dollar tech industry is quietly reshaping desire, intimacy and love. Kantayya digs into how dating platforms are designed to maximize engagement and profit, often at the expense of authentic human connection. The film raises questions about agency, autonomy, privacy, and the commercialization of human intimacy. “I’ve watched Big Tech move from capturing our attention to shaping our most intimate human relationships. ‘Love Apptually’ asks whether the loneliness epidemic is a consequence of technological design,” said director Shalini Kantayya. The film bowed at Hot Docs and also recently screened at DOC NYC. “Love Apptually” marks the final installment in Kantayya’s trilogy examining technology’s impact on human experience, following “Coded Bias” and “TikTok, Boom.,” which both premiered at Sundance, screened on PBS’s Independent Lens and received Emmy nominations. “Valentine’s Day is a time when we celebrate love, but ‘Love Apptually’ asks us to look more closely at the forces shaping how we find it,” said Elizabeth Woodward, founder and CEO of Willa and producer of the film. “Shalini has created a film that reveals how technology has moved beyond capturing our attention to influencing our most intimate relationships. We’re excited to bring the film to audiences at a moment when these conversations feel particularly meaningful, and to use the theatrical experience as an opportunity to reconnect, reflect, and rethink what it means to find love in the digital age.” “We have worked with Shalini Kantayya since her first film, ‘A Drop of Life,’ and we were proud to support ‘Love Apptually’ through our Production Assistance Program,” says Debra Zimmerman, executive director of Women Make Movies. “After the phenomenal success and tremendous impact of ‘Coded Bias,’ including screenings with decision makers at major technology companies, we’re eager to work with Willa to help audiences everywhere see the film and continue these conversations.”

blocks.text: ‘Love Apptually’ is a 7th Empire Media production, presented by Willa in association with Minderoo Pictures and the Concordia Fellowship, with support from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation and the Perspective Fund. The film is produced by Kantayya and Woodward. Executive producers include Davis Guggenheim, Rahdi Taylor, Doron Weber, and Malinda Wink, with co-executive producers Meryl Metni, Natasha Dolby and David Dolby.
